accepted_for: referable diabetic retinopathy (ICDR grade >= 2) ranking only
claim: Ranks fundus photographs by likelihood of referable diabetic retinopathy (ICDR grade >= 2) so a human reviewer sees higher-risk images sooner. A triage and prioritisation aid. Every image in the queue is still reviewed by a person; the model changes the order, not the outcome.
what_this_does_not_claim: NOT a refer / no-refer decision. At 90% sensitivity the model flags 70% of all images and its positive predictive value at EyePACS's real 19.6% prevalence is 0.353 -- roughly two referrals in three would be unnecessary. Lowering sensitivity to 80% only reaches 0.506. No threshold makes this a decision rule.

NOT mild-DR detection. Grade 1 versus grade 0 is a different task, measured separately at AUC 0.660 [0.617, 0.703] within-source and 0.5850 cross-source. Roadmap steps 5 and 6 established that neither more data nor backbone adaptation moves it. It is not usable and is not covered here.
NOT five-grade DR severity grading. On this same evaluation set the model scores exact-grade accuracy 0.267 and quadratic weighted kappa 0.460. It cannot assign a grade.

NOT glaucoma, cataract, AMD, hypertension, myopia or any other ocular condition. Those outputs exist in the network but are not validated: their apparently strong external figures are within-source (every surviving external image of those classes comes from ODIR, which is in training).

NOT a diagnosis, and NOT a calibrated probability. The score ranks; it does not estimate risk. Brier 0.268, 46.9% of scores below 0.01, and every threshold reaching 80-95% sensitivity lies between 0.000 and 0.005 -- a default 0.5 cut would refer almost nothing.
NOT validated on any population other than EyePACS. One external source, US-based, single-grader ICDR labels, no adjudicated subset.
evaluation_scope: Frozen EyePACS external manifest, n=1,500, never trained on, a different acquisition source from APTOS and ODIR which are both in training. Manifest pinned at backend/data/processed/eye/eyepacs_external_manifest.csv and verified by fingerprint on every scoring run.

metrics.why_ppv_is_here: Because the AUC alone reads as a screening result and this number is what shows it is not one. Two referrals in three would be unnecessary at a clinically ordinary sensitivity.
metrics.why_enrichment_is_here: Because it is the capability that is actually supported. Sorted by score at real prevalence, the top fifth of the queue holds 71.2% of referable disease -- a reviewer working top-down finds most of what matters in a fifth of the time, and discharges nobody.

operating_point.why_not: Every candidate threshold in the capability report was read off the same frozen set the model is scored on; choosing one there and quoting its sensitivity would be selection on the test data. A deployment threshold must be fixed on a separate selection set. Until then the module ships a ranking and no verdict.

limitations: No operating point is selected. Every threshold above was read off this same set; choosing one here and quoting its sensitivity would be selection on the test data. A deployment threshold must be fixed on a separate selection set before any promotion.
PPV on this set is inflated. It is 60% referable by construction against 19.6% in full EyePACS, so the per-threshold PPV at natural prevalence is the honest figure and is reported beside it.
One external source. EyePACS is US-based; the module has no measured performance on any other unseen population.
Single-image, single-field. No stereo, no fundus pairs, no clinical context, and no assessment of image-quality gating in deployment.
Nondeterminism: inference on this GPU drifts run to run at roughly 1e-5 AUC (roadmap step 1). Immaterial here, but it means figures quoted to four decimals from a single run are over-precise.
Grade labels are EyePACS's own single-grader ICDR labels, which are known to carry grader noise; no adjudicated subset was available.

THE SCORE IS NOT CALIBRATED. It ranks well but is not a probability: Brier 0.268, 46.9% of scores below 0.01, and the thresholds reaching 80-95% sensitivity all sit between 0.000 and 0.005. A default 0.5 cut would refer almost nothing. The raw number must never be displayed as a percentage risk, and calibration on a separate set is a prerequisite for any deployment, not a refinement.

THE INPUT GATE CANNOT VERIFY THE IMAGE IS A FUNDUS PHOTOGRAPH. It checks resolution, brightness and blur, but a dermoscopy image or a face photograph passes and receives a referable-DR ranking score. Two candidate heuristics were measured and both failed: near-black surround fraction (fundus DDR reaches 0.000, identical to dermoscopy) and red/green ratio (fundus median 1.42-1.94 against dermoscopy 1.46 -- fully overlapping). No threshold separates them without rejecting genuine fundus images, so none was invented. The caller is responsible for sending fundus photographs, and the served response says so.

served_input_gate.what_it_is: An input-modality safety gate, NOT a diagnostic model. It decides only whether an uploaded image is a fundus photograph, and makes no clinical claim.
served_input_gate.why_it_is_part_of_the_served_path: Without it the referable-DR model scored dermoscopy at median 0.9828 against genuine referable fundus at 0.0145, and 100% of dermoscopy images landed in the top 20% of a ranked review queue (faces 55%). A misrouted skin photo outranked nearly every real referable case and displaced genuine disease from the priority band this module is accepted to serve.
served_input_gate.order_of_operations: validate_input_quality -> modality gate -> referable-DR model. A rejected input raises before preprocessing and never invokes the DR model.
served_input_gate.model: EfficientNet-B0, 224x224, 5-way (fundus, dermoscopy, face, jaundice_sclera, other); serving decision is binary on P(fundus)
served_input_gate.threshold_provenance: Pre-registered: selected on a selection split under a 0.5% false-rejection target, locked, then the held-out set scored exactly once. Not re-tuned afterwards.
served_input_gate.honest_caveat: The 0.67% point estimate is under the 1% ceiling, but its Wilson interval [0.26%, 1.70%] still CONTAINS 1%. 600 fundus images cannot resolve 0.67% from 1.00%. What the rerun changed is which side of the line the estimate falls on, not the precision of the measurement. Roughly 1 in 150 genuine fundus images will be turned away and the user asked to retry.
known_limitations: jaundice_sclera and other are cluster-disjoint, not source-disjoint; neither has a second independent source on disk.
other is synthetic and says nothing about real-world junk uploads.
One acquisition source per class on the held-out side, so nothing measures an unseen camera or dermatoscope.
It gates modality, not image quality. The resolution, brightness and blur checks still do that job, and run first.
If its weights cannot load, the module refuses rather than passing inputs through unscreened.

served_output_constrained.note: eye_model.predict was narrowed in the same change that set this flag. It previously emitted a dr_grade_N label and all eight disease probabilities; promoting it unchanged would have shipped a five-grade grader and an eight-condition classifier on a referable-DR-only validation.
served_output_constrained.input_screening: a modality gate runs before the DR model; non-fundus images are refused with an input-quality message and never scored
now_emits: a single referable-DR priority score, labelled as a ranking
risk_score: null -- the score is uncalibrated and the UI renders that field as a percentage risk bar
warnings carrying the scope limits above
modality_fundus_probability and modality_gate_threshold in handcrafted_features, so a response shows the gate ran
no_longer_emits: glaucoma / cataract / amd / hypertension / myopia / other / normal probabilities
